![US President Donald Trump speaks during the United Nations General Assembly in New York last week. Photo: Getty Images / TNS](https://cdn.i-scmp.com/sites/default/files/styles/1020x680/public/d8/images/canvas/2026/09/28/96b18986-33c0-4b85-8c48-a65cf779d809_76f2dd7e.jpg?itok=OIKnW7Ih&v=1790536410)

[Agence France-Presse](/author/agence-france-presse-1)

US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he expects talks with Iran to resume in the coming week, despite his rejection of a truce proposal put forward by Tehran.

Iranian officials brought with them to the UN General Assembly in New York a plan for a seven-day truce followed by the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz shipping channel.

Trump dismissed the plan and has mused on resuming full-scale air strikes on Iranian targets but he told the news platform Axios that he expects negotiations to resume.

“They want to make a deal but it is not the deal that I want to make,” Trump told Axios. “It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago.”

Peace negotiators are pressing Iran to make a concession on its nuclear program to revive ceasefire talks with the U.S. after President Trump rejected Tehran’s truce proposal, in a race to stop the conflict from escalating back into all-out war.

Mediators involved in the talks said it is a long-shot bid to get Iran to placate Trump on the issue he cares about most. Trump has tried to reframe the conflict around his original war goal of preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon, and redirect talks away from unlocking the Strait of Hormuz from Iran’s grip. In a speech to the United Nations last week, Trump said he was weighing whether to “annihilate” Iran’s government to keep it from gaining a nuclear bomb.

# Iran Seeks U.S. Clarification After Trump Rejects Cease-Fire Proposal

Abbas Araghchi, Iran’s foreign minister, said a history of contradictory messaging meant that President Trump’s rebuff might not be a final position.

Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, has said his country would wait for mediators to communicate the U.S. response to its latest cease-fire proposal before abandoning efforts to restart talks about the plan, despite President Trump’s public rejection of it.

Mr. Trump told reporters on Saturday that the proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route in the Persian Gulf, and restart talks about Iran’s nuclear program within seven days “would not be acceptable,” although he signaled he was open to negotiations.

Mr. Araghchi, who is still in New York after last week’s annual U.N. General Assembly, brushed off the Mr. Trump’s rebuff as typical of the president’s conflicting messaging.

“The U.S. President has said some good things as well as many contradictory things, which unfortunately we hear from him quite often,” the foreign minister said in a statement on social media on Saturday. “We are waiting for the definitive views to be conveyed to us through the intermediaries, and we will make a decision on that basis.”

# German, Russian foreign ministers hold rare talks amid rising tensions

*Russia’s top diplomat Lavrov dismisses German Foreign Minister Wadephul’s call to abandon ‘dangerous path of escalation’ with Europe.*

Save

Share

![Minister of Foreign Affairs Johann David Wadephul of Germany speaks during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly at United Nations headquarters, Saturday, September 26, 2026 [Heather Khalifa/AP)](/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/AP26269641599869-1790475976.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul speaks during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City on September 26, 2026 [Heather Khalifa/AP)

By AFP, AP and Reuters

Published On 27 Sep 202627 Sep 2026

Germany’s Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has called on Russia to abandon its “dangerous path of escalation” with Germany, Europe and NATO during talks with his Russian counterpart, Sergey Lavrov, in New York.

The meeting on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly on Saturday — the first such talks since Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine — was requested by the German side, according to Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova. It was held before Lavrov’s address to world leaders.

# Trump-Xi Summit: Key Outcomes and Implications

[Geopolitechs](https://substack.com/@geotechnopolitics)

The eight outcomes released by the Chinese side begin with the establishment of a **constructive and strategically stable China-U.S. relationship based on respect, fairness and reciprocity**. This is followed, in order, by mutual support for APEC and the G20; Iran’s commitment not to develop nuclear weapons; recognition of China and the United States as World War II allies; the bilateral economic and trade consultation mechanism and its outcomes, including reciprocal tariff reductions covering US$30 billion worth of trade; joint counternarcotics law enforcement; the AI dialogue; and the arrival of giant pandas in the United States.

The U.S. side placed counternarcotics cooperation and the loan of giant pandas to the United States in the first two positions, followed by trade and investment in third place and the constructive and strategically stable relationship in fourth. These were followed by mutual support for APEC and the G20, preventing Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons, recognition of the two countries’ World War II alliance, and the AI dialogue.

The same eight outcomes therefore appear in a different order in the two lists. China leads with the overall framework for the bilateral relationship, while the United States puts counternarcotics, pandas, and trade and investment first. This reflects different priorities in how the two sides publicly present the outc
